'survived' means all 8 still passed, i.e. the unit does not pin that guard. || repair139 added probes PA-PG; the 2026-09-16 rotation pass added PH. || 2026-09-16 correction: this note said 7 tests; the file declares 8 [Test] methods and every case runs 8, so the count was raised to 8 to match the run. An unmutated baseline case has no mutant to escape and is reported as baseline_passed/baseline_failed, never as 'survived'. || 2026-09-16 rotation scope: the three frames in foundation/world/connected-world-profile.json carry yaw 0, 0 and 180, and sin(0) = sin(180) = 0, so the sine terms of SpatialFrame.ToWorld/ToLocal are algebraically inert in every authored frame. M12 and M13 are caught through the cosine term and do not show the sine term is pinned; probe PH drops the sine term alone and is the case that does. The yaw 90 assertions it is caught by were added to FrameConsistencyMatchesAuthoritativeResponseAcrossAllSurfaces in this same file, which is the file this harness compiles.

mutations.note: ConnectedWorldDefinition.cs:17-18 negate both terms of the ToWorld Z row (Origin.Z - s * local.X + c * local.Z becomes Origin.Z + s * local.X - c * local.Z). This is NOT a pure yaw-sign flip and is NOT limited to non-zero yaw: the cosine term is negated too, so it is observable at yaw 0 as well. Measured for local.Z = -3.75: the Z term moves from -3.750 to +3.750 at yaw 0, at yaw 90 and at yaw 180 alike. The narrower defect that is genuinely invisible at yaw 0 is the dropped sine term, which is recorded separately as PH.

replacements.new:

ConnectedWorldDefinition.cs:17-18 drop the sine term from SpatialFrame.ToWorld while leaving the cosine term intact (Origin.X + c * local.X + s * local.Z becomes Origin.X + c * local.X, and the matching Z row loses - s * local.X). This is the narrower defect M12 and M13 cannot express: both of those also disturb the cosine term, and every frame in the authored table has sin(yaw) = 0, so before this probe no case in this file could distinguish a frame transform that carries rotation from one that ignores it. It is caught by the yaw 90 assertions added to FrameConsistencyMatchesAuthoritativeResponseAcrossAllSurfaces for exactly this case. ToLocal is deliberately left unmutated, so the round trip assertion fails alongside the two axis assertions.

                Origin.Z - s * local.X + c * local.Z);
replacements.new:
